title: Fly to Shandur, the world's highest polo ground
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: High in the Hindu Kush and Karakoram, between Chitral and Gilgit-Baltistan, lies the Shandur Pass.
Let's fly up from the Laspur valley, on the Chitral side.
The road climbs to a wide, open plateau, about three thousand seven hundred metres above sea level.
Here lies Shandur Lake, and beside it, a flat meadow that hosts the highest polo ground in the world.
Every summer, thousands of visitors come here for the Shandur Polo Festival, a tradition that dates back to nineteen thirty-six.
Teams from Chitral and Gilgit-Baltistan face each other in one of the fiercest rivalries in sport.
They play freestyle mountain polo, one of the oldest surviving forms of the game, with very few rules.
This year, Gilgit-Baltistan beat Chitral six-five in the final, their first title in more than a decade.
The festival also brings folk music, traditional dances, local food and handicrafts to the top of the pass.
Polo is often called the game of kings, but at Shandur it belongs to the mountain communities.
This year's festival was held in June, in the short summer season, when the pass is easiest to reach.
